a.q: Which is 8:45 pm written in 24-hour time?
a.why: 8:45 pm is between 1:00 pm and 11:59 pm, so add 12 to the hour: \(8 + 12 = 20\), giving 20:45. The option 08:45 keeps the hour unchanged, which is only right for an am time.
a.clue: The hour is a pm hour after 1:00 pm, so something is added.

b.q: Sam in Melbourne phones a friend in Perth at 19:30 Melbourne time. During daylight saving, Perth is 3 hours behind Melbourne. What time is it in Perth, in 12-hour time?
b.why: Perth is behind, so subtract 3 hours: 19:30 becomes 16:30. Subtracting 12 from the hour gives 4:30 pm. Adding 3 hours gives 22:30, which is 10:30 pm, but that moves the wrong way.
b.clue: Behind means an earlier time. Then change 24-hour time back.

draft.title: Time zones and 24-hour time
card: 24-hour time counts hours from 0 to 23 with no am or pm. For am times up to 12:59 pm, the hour stays the same, except 12:00 am (midnight) is 00:00. From 1:00 pm, add 12 to the hour, so 3:15 pm is 15:15.
To go back to 12-hour time, subtract 12 from any hour above 12. So 21:40 is 9:40 pm.
To find a duration, count from the start time to the end time. From 14:30 to 17:10 is 2 hours 40 minutes: 30 minutes to 15:00, then 2 hours to 17:00, then 10 minutes.

A place east of another is ahead, so its clock shows a later time. A place west is behind. To change zone, add hours going to a place that is ahead and subtract hours going to a place that is behind. Example: Perth is 3 hours behind Melbourne (in the same season), so when it is 15:00 in Melbourne it is 12:00 in Perth.
draft.remember: Add 12 to pm hours for 24-hour time. Add hours going ahead, subtract going behind.

problems.detail: Perth is 3 hours behind Melbourne only while Victoria is on daylight saving (AEDT, UTC+11 vs AWST, UTC+8). In winter the gap is 2 hours. 'In the same season' wrongly implies the gap is always 3 hours. Say it is 3 hours during daylight saving, or 2 hours in winter.

'For am times up to 12:59 pm, the hour stays the same' mixes am and pm and is confusing. 'Except 12:00 am (midnight) is 00:00' also suggests only exactly 12:00 am changes, when every 12:xx am time becomes 00:xx.
'Add 12 to pm hours' is wrong for 12:xx pm times, which stay as 12:xx. The card correctly says 'from 1:00 pm', so the remember line overgeneralises it.
